title: Measles deaths pass 1,300; three of the latest five were in Sylhet
excerpt: Five more people died with measles symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on 13 November, bringing the toll since mid-March to 1,304.

image.alt: Ward blocks at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, including its paediatric unit
image.credit: Nahid Hossain / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Five more people died with measles symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on Friday, 13 November, three of them in Sylhet division and one each in Dhaka and Mymensingh, according to DGHS data reported by bdnews24.com and The Business Standard. Deaths since 15 March now stand at 1,304.

The numbers

  • Deaths: 1,304, of which 1,199 were suspected measles and 105 laboratory-confirmed.
  • Suspected cases: 245,562, including 1,271 in the latest 24 hours.
  • Confirmed cases: 25,028, including 148 in the latest 24 hours.
  • Hospital admissions: 219,247 suspected patients since 15 March, of whom 210,401 have recovered.
  • Deaths by division: Dhaka 535, Sylhet 213, Chattogram 120, Rajshahi 93, Mymensingh 93, Barishal 70, Khulna 57, Rangpur 18.

Devlens reported 1,289 deaths on 10 November, so 15 more deaths have been recorded in three days.

Why it matters

Sylhet has the second highest death toll of any division despite a much smaller population than Dhaka, and it accounted for most of the latest deaths. Organisations working there can help trace children who missed doses and get sick children to hospital early.

What to watch

Whether new suspected cases drop below 1,000 a day, and whether the government targets a catch-up vaccination round at Sylhet division.

Sources
